title: Round 35 New Hampshire-Vermont state-frame USGS GNIS source register
scope: All-GNIS starter registers for New Hampshire and Vermont. Every seeded row reproduces one USGS GNIS record screened by exact official name, returned type/state/county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and returned GNIS primary point, and cross-checked on two independent USGS surfaces (USGS GNIS Geocoder; staged-products DomesticNames text via tools/gnis_extract.py; cumulative candidate extract resources/city-subsurface/gnis-candidates-batch7.json with per-state ZIP SHA-256 values). Mount Washington and Mount Mansfield carry Domestic Names per-ID identity checks. The Monadnock name order, the Saint Johnsbury spelling, and the empty Connecticut/Merrimack/Saco main-stem screens are recorded below.

usgsGeocoder.use: Fuzzy candidate discovery only. A candidate was accepted only when Name, Type, State, County, GnisId, Latitude, and Longitude all matched the intended feature and the point lay inside the intended state. County records, census-designated places, historical records, airport/bay/cape/valley records, and same-name records of another class or county were rejected explicitly where relevant. Screens use the official GNIS name (Monadnock Mountain; Saint Johnsbury; Camels Hump).

gnisDomesticNames.use: Second-surface cross-check of every seeded FEATURE_ID and per-ID identity checks for Mount Washington (871352) and Mount Mansfield (1461774), extracted in a GitHub Actions runner by tools/gnis_extract.py. The current text layout carries no elevation columns, so the summit elevations cite USGS-published state-highpoint values. The candidate extract file is cumulative across batches 7-17; this register is the frozen batch-17 evidence.

selectionRules: VERIFIED=1 is claimed only for an exact official name, compatible GNIS feature class/type, intended state and returned primary county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and an official point returned by a cited USGS service, reproduced identically on the second USGS surface.
Grouped Geocoder Types map explicitly to stored row classes: Cities & Populated Places to Populated Place, Lakes & Reservoirs to Lake, Streams & Canals to Stream, and Summit to Summit.
A stored GNIS primary point is never described as a municipal boundary, street-address geocode, generic centroid, shoreline polygon, summit outline, or river centerline.

If exact-name candidates remain indistinguishable, or the state-filtered screen returns no intended feature record, the feature is omitted from that state gazetteer and may appear only as a generalized context corridor (Connecticut and Merrimack main stems in both frames this batch; Saco in New Hampshire).
Statewide frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized corridors; no bundled DEM or surveyed boundary is implied.

newhampshire.title: New Hampshire statewide frame (New Hampshire-Vermont batch)
newhampshire.frameNote: New Hampshire-Vermont batch: the Concord capital anchor is balanced with the per-ID Mount Washington high point (6,288 ft), Monadnock Mountain under its GNIS name order, three lakes (Winnipesaukee, Squam, Umbagog), and the Piscataqua mouth record. The Connecticut, Merrimack, Saco, and Androscoggin main stems return no NH Stream record (reservoir impoundments or empty screens) and remain corridors.

identityDecisions.candidate: Connecticut River under states=NH and states=VT (no Stream record)
identityDecisions.decision: Corridor-only in both frames. Both state screens return only features named Connecticut River Reservoir (Lakes & Reservoirs class); no Stream record for the main stem is returned under NH or VT, so no river row is seeded in either frame and the river is drawn as a generalized corridor along each frame's boundary edge.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The corridor lines are not channel centerlines or surveyed state boundaries.

identityDecisions.candidate: Merrimack River and Saco River and Androscoggin River under states=NH
identityDecisions.decision: Not seeded. The Merrimack and Androscoggin screens return only River Reservoir impoundment records under NH, and the Saco screen is empty; their main-stem GNIS records key to their Maine/Massachusetts mouths. All three remain context corridors where drawn.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: Corridor treatment is not a claim that New Hampshire lacks these rivers.

identityDecisions.decision: Seeded under the official GNIS name order Monadnock Mountain (Cheshire County Summit). The familiar Mount Monadnock order screened empty under states=NH.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The seeded point is not a summit outline.

identityDecisions.decision: GNIS spells the name Saint Johnsbury in full; the row is stored under that official spelling (Center and CDP records rejected).
identityDecisions.notClaimed: No abbreviation is implied for local usage.

identityDecisions.decision: GNIS spells the summit Camels Hump without an apostrophe; stored verbatim.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The seeded point is not a summit outline.

identityDecisions.candidate: Lake Champlain GNIS point (Grand Isle County, VT-associated record)
identityDecisions.decision: Seeded in Vermont on the VT-associated record returned for states=VT. The point sits in the Grand Isle reach; most of the lake lies west of the frame in New York.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The stored point is not a shoreline, centroid, or state boundary.

knownLimitations: New Hampshire and Vermont are starter registers, not statewide GNIS extracts. Each contains 12 deliberately selected identity-safe rows.

The USGS Geocoder is a suggestion service; exact-match screening by official name/type/state/county/FEATURE_ID is part of the evidence. Every seeded row was reproduced on the second USGS surface (staged-products DomesticNames text) at the same primary point.

The current DomesticNames text layout carries no elevation columns, so Mount Washington (6,288 feet) and Mount Mansfield (4,395 feet) elevations cite USGS-published values; GNIS identity rests on the per-ID class/county/point reproduction.

GNIS point data do not supply the displayed terrain or corridors. Both frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized context lines; the Green Mountain and White Mountain amplitudes are illustrative, not a DEM.

State frames are rectangles, not state-boundary clipping masks. Both rectangles include neighbouring-state land and (for Vermont) part of Lake Champlain and Canada-adjacent waters; no boundary geometry is claimed.
